name: LHCO control-region collider anomalies
description: fit(control_features) -> object with score(events). Input consists of pinned physics features derived from official LHCO Pythia/Delphes events; candidate never receives signal truth. Independent training, test and no-signal source event blocks. Score SIC at 5 percent background divided by one plus mass-sculpting chi-square. Report no-signal acceptance and AUROC; no discovery p value.

limitations: Independent SCIEL adaptation, not a reproduction of source leaderboard scores.
Candidate and evaluator share a Python process. Input APIs withhold labels but do not provide an OS security boundary; isolate evaluation data for adversarial use.
Bounded first50,000 author-shuffled R&D source events. Training retains actual source signal contamination; no detector-observation discovery or cross-generator generalization claim.
Retrieved byte ranges and normalized pack are SHA256-verified. Full-source advertised MD5 is preserved but not claimed verified after partial download.

papers.title: Classifying anomalies through outer density estimation
papers.task_relation: The local task uses LHCO events, unlabeled control-region training, and significance improvement with a mass-sculpting penalty. Its fixed features and scoring are narrower than the published method and do not constitute an experimental discovery search.
papers.primary_goal: Improve resonant anomaly searches through data-driven background estimation using sidebands.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Identify possible new-physics resonances without requiring a specific signal model or sculpting a false mass peak.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Model-independent collider searches are the central physics-search objective of the cited anomaly-detection method.
science_relevance.reason: The paper proposes a solution to a specific new-physics search problem, beyond documenting an anomaly benchmark.
